Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise EDIT: initially I reviewed this before really getting into the puzzle. I’m in it now, and I can say this is one of the most poorly formulated puzzles I’ve ever done. It appears that whoever decided the pattern of the piece cut outs was lazy and decided to have repeating shapes throughout, which results in many perfect fits that are completely incorrect. In places where the differences are obvious, it’s not much of an issue, but there are also plenty of times this happens in areas that look similar, resulting in incorrect placement, backtracking, and frustration. I love puzzles, but not this one. I love friends, but I can’t stand this friends puzzle. The visual design was excellent, so whoever came up with that did a wonderful job. Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

So the puzzle itself isn’t super high res, nor are the pieces particularly inventive in how they’re cut, but man am I having fun reliving the show. Honestly, this is all about the nostalgia and having a chill time. It’s a little harder than I expected, but still totally doable. Perfect escape!
text_fidelity_b: Friends TV Show Collage Jigsaw Puzzle 1000 Pieces Officially Licensed Friends TV Show Merchandise

text_fidelity_a:
Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!
text_fidelity_b: Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma

Hot Wheels Track Set with 1:64 Scale Toy Firetruck, City Fire Station with Dragon Nemesis and Track Play, Dragon Drive Firefight We've owned plenty of hotwheels sets, some pretty standard and some pretty creative. This is one of those interesting ones I couldn't really understand until we got it. The car is sort of on an "assisted loop", in that there are points that require your intervention to continue. It starts off being "spit out" by the dragon, then fired from a booth, then launched up a loop, and- if everything goes according to plan - it lands on the head of the dragon which will either fall forward or to the side (not knowing which way is part of the fun). However, if you don't have everything 100% seated properly, it just fails miserably. My kids had trouble getting it to work until I came and reseated some parts more forcefully, but even then we still had a few misfires that caused it not to work.
But I suppose that's the tradeoff of the more obscure track sets, sometimes they are more difficult to operate successfully. Part of the fun is making it work, I think. But if you have a kid who isn't up for that challenge, maybe this isn't the set for them. We actually really liked it, and the payoff when it DOES work is the sort of moment that gets high fives and cheers all around.

text_fidelity_a:
Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size This is a really great idea for a children's bank and the top part, the counter, works really well. Unfortunately, there are a number of things here that made it not really work for my family. At least not at this time.

First, with little children in the house, the top buttons get pressed accidentally or on purpose when they are not supposed to and so the count has not been correct for that reason. I almost would've preferred some other method of managing bills and kept this as a coin counter only so that you have the immediate feedback putting something in, seeing the number change, and knowing that it's accurate. This would not be an issue in households only with bigger kids who can control themselves from pushing buttons inappropriately, but definitely made it not workable in my house during these years.

Next, I really hoped that the cool top would have threads so that they could fit on a mason jar of any size, so while the little ones are tiny they can have a little chart, and as they grow older they can have a large jar, but unfortunately it does not work with any size mason jar – the sizing, the threads, and the lip that hangs over are all totally different.

Lastly, and this is my main issue, the cheap, foggy, and unattractive plastic container that holds all of the money is so lightweight and is angled weird so that if there are primarily bills with only a few coins in there, the whole thing gets really top-heavy and wants to tip over. My son primarily gets money through finding change on the ground and through getting dollars or 20s on his birthday or Christmas. So there are a few coins in there, sure, but mostly single bills sent from afar through the mail. Had they made the top interchangeable with Mason jars, this would have been an issue because I just would put the whole thing on nice glass mason jar, probably one of those colored blue, purple, or green ones that they've come out with in recent years. Alas, you're really stuck with just the plastic container that the lid fits on. This limits how long anybody would want to use something like this, because I think most teenagers have slightly better taste than to want some cheap plastic thing of a single specific size sitting in their bedroom.

That said, for a very specific age range and if you don't have smaller children around the house, this could work really well and be a very fun way of having kids learn about saving and making it rewarding.
text_fidelity_b: Ben Franklin Toys Electronic Bill & Coin Counter Bank with LCD Screen, One Size

Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

AMIGO X-Code Cooperative Strategy Board Game, Black This is very different from anything we have played before. It is very quick to learn and very quick to play. I love that it is cooperative which keeps most hurt feelings down. It played well at a range of ages from 11 to 51 which was also fantastic. All in all, I am very impressed with this game.

The play is very easy...at first. Basically, you are passing cards to help each other make sets and cover the numbers on a phone keypad. There are rules governing how to pass and who to pass too and lots of communication as you try to get cards where they need to go. You can also make sets of cards that allow you to extend your game by flipping your one minute timer. We found the first round pretty easy actually, and then came the twists... It has a good variety of challenges that make a nice straight forward game more challenging.

I highly recommend this game. There are few games that can be learned so quickly, play accross some many ages, and be so fun and engaging. They hit it all on this one.

I wish that instead of selfishly trying to go for increase brand recognition, they would've found something cute to put on there instead, like a star, heart, or cat face. Other than that, this is a really cute set that is fun as is, or fun to mix and match with other glitter girls outfits in this line.

Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

Monopoly Junior: Disney Pixar Cars 3 Edition A nice update to an old game. I threw this in my shopping cart while out Christmas shopping. So I did not buy it on Amazon, but I am an Amazon Prime member. Cars 3 Monopoly Jr. is played just like regular Monopoly Jr. Only the pieces, property names, and chance cards have a Cars 3 theme. The rules are exactly the same. For those of you who do not know, Monopoly Jr. is a simplified version of Monopoly. You don't build houses or hotels. Mortgages on property is not a thing. The money is also way more simple. You still go to "jail." You will collect $2. However, there is literally no strategy involved. Just be the one to have the most money once one person goes bankrupt and you win. Monopoly Jr. does not end in arguments or tears (so long as your child can handle the issue of losing, which I will explain later.) Monopoly Jr. will not be the source of a deep rift through the family. You will find that you're still friends with people after the game is over. Game play is fast, you will not be playing into the wee hours of the morning trying to negotiate a loan because you landed on Park Place.

I like board games because it gets me and my son together and playing together. Screens are not involved. However, do understand that teaching 3-5 year olds how to play board games is a long process. At the end of the day, the point of playing games like this with kids this young is to get them using various skills. Skills such as paying attention, following multiple steps, counting, and taking turns. I would recommend holding off on competitive board games until after you have played a few cooperative board games. Such as [[ASIN:B006S9MUPU Peaceable Kingdom / Race to the Treasure! Cooperative Board Game]] or [[ASIN:B002V3RCE6 Wonder Forge Richard Scarry's Busytown, Eye Found It]] Why? Because I found it helpful to play cooperative style games after playing competitive games ended in broken pieces and a broken spirit. text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Busy Island Set The pictures I've shared show three different Thomas train sets and the new wood style of connector. The sets pictured in the photos I've included are the busy island set, the farm set, and the park set that just has a circular track included with the figure, a park bench, and the Thomas. Any of these sets on their own would not be quite enough to get kids started. My main complaint about all of the sets is that they don't include enough tracks. They have a lot of interesting and exciting components, but it takes a lot of hard work and thought to get all of the components together with the small number of tracks that are included, and then you don't get to build and rebuild as much as you'd like because there simply are not that many track configurations that actually work with the small number of straight tracks and curves included.

As for the new style of connector, many people have commented that this seems like a cash grab to make it so that you cannot use your old tracks. Fisher-Price continually says that with the included connectors, you can just connect up to your old style of track. Both of these complaints are a little bit right. The new track style has some things going for it and other things that are not my favorite. The thing going for it is that the tracks do connect together much more sturdily, and I really appreciate that this makes for a smoother run on the tracks than with brio and all of the other brands that use the other connection standard. Every set that you get from Thomas has two converters, and so in theory if you have an existing wooden Thomas set with the old connectors, you can connect up two different runs of the train with these couple of connectors, but you can't really integrate them all very well, and using the connectors and keeping the two types of train area distinct are something that smaller children will have issues with.

As for how it is to play with, my five-year-old loves how sturdy the connections are and how easy it is to build with them. My three-year-old finds it hard to get the pieces apart because you need to do a very clean hold and pull upward motion which I find very easy, my five-year-old finds very easy, but my three-year-old wants to pull apart while pulling up, and that little bit of motion of trying to pull them apart sideways makes it so that it is very tough for her to get them apart. Hopefully this will be something that clicks for her soon and she will be able to play with the trains independently. We've only had the set for less than a week.

The busy island set specifically is probably the number one set that you would want and need to get if you are getting the Fisher-Price wood set going. It has so many fun implements, an airport, the ferry boat which connects up to the train station, the little bridge piece with some water around it to where you can lift the bridge and let the ferry go through, giraffes and zebras and some little fenced areas with grass for them to go, some interesting diverter tracks that let you choose which direction the trains go, and a few fun trains, dual level supporting pieces, and just enough tracks to put it all together.

You will definitely need to buy additional sets or additional track packs in order to make this truly fun to play with and not just something the set up once and run your trains around.

The busy island set was definitely the one that included the most diverse and interesting pieces for play. The farm set was an exciting addition, but basically just added some more track pieces, some more fenced areas, some farm animals and an egg selling stand, and the dual level farm. These are all interesting pieces, but in all honesty doesn't offer a ton more play besides the imaginative variety. I definitely recommend getting it also, but the busy island set is the first one to get because it has the most interesting options for varied play.

Overall, we are delighted with this set and you probably could've heard my kids whooping with joy about a mile away when I pulled it out of the box and they realized just what was inside. We haven't done any other train sets yet, but my three-year-old has had so much fun with some tiny little roadbuilding toys that I thought she would particularly benefit from this, and I knew my five-year-old would also love it.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Busy Island Set

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments I used to work in Microbiology and one job in particular pertained to streaking for bacteria and viruses on various types of agar plates. We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!

text_fidelity_a:
Black+Decker Kids Workbench - Power Tools Workshop - Build Your Own Toy Tool Box – 75 Realistic Toy Tools and Accessories [Amazon Exclusive] I'm disappointed in this workbench. Knowing I would eventually want to get our boy a tool bench, I started shopping for one when he was just when he was a newborn. After carefully reviewing every bench on the market, this seemed like the best one, based on the reviews on several sites.

But here are some of the reasons why I am disappointed:
- The vice (vise) grip no longer opens and closes like in the previous version.
- the nails and screws don't stay up on their own, you put them in the holes and they sink immediately (which completely defeats the purpose of pounding them down with a hammer).
- the batteries are already drained in the saw and drill press, and it hasn't even been out of the box for a month.
- the drill press lights are too bright and flash rapidly... seizure anyone???
- as you'll notice from the other uploaded pictures, the hooks that hang on the tools (like the screw driver, hammer, etc) fall out immediately.
- the storage shelf underneath is incredibly shallow; you really can't store anything of the extra pieces down there. And even the slightest play motion from your toddler will knock everything off of the lower shelf.

So with all that said, it still gets 3 stars because our 24 month old plays with it several times a day.

And another FYI: The last two years, the mega chain store with the bulls-eye logo has put this toy on sale during Black Friday weekend for $40 dollars, so Amazon drops their price too. For $40, it was an ok buy.... but for the $60 dollars it is listed for now (or for the $80 it was listed for in the weeks on Amazon prior to black Friday), I feel like this was completely over-priced. You'd be better off watching craig's list or finding it at a re-sale shop for the equally-as-good used version for around $25-30. text_fidelity_a:
4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8 I only paid $10 for this so I wasn't expecting lots, however I was expecting it to be decently made and a little more as described.

Putting that aside, if you plan to buy this I suggest you carefully look over the box and "in use" photos. On the box it does say you have to put the robot together and that it's meant for children over 8, those are very key points that I see were missed as I read the reviews. I wish I'd have really looked at the pictures myself, because I was expecting solid lines, not a bunch of dots, and from the given discription I thought the patterns would be more than just repeated crappy circles, also something you kind of see if you look at the pictures. Although even if you notice the pictures show dots and not lines, my dots were very widely spaced.

The things I couldn't have known from the pictures is how crappy it really is. The clear dome is thinner than your average disposable water bottle, everything that can be is shoddy plastic, and there is zero quality control. The wires on the one I got were attached to the wrong sides, thankfully they left the naked wires too long or it wouldn't have been useable at all because they needed to be crossed behind the motor to work at all. Plus, while this is technically buildable by children, the nuts, bolts and screws are so small that they are tricky to handle even for adults. It isn't hard to build at all, barely having enough parts to really be called buildable, so it isn't all that fantastic at what it's supposed to be, something to encourage children to think, build and experiment. Honestly if they included alternate uses or ways you can experiment with this it would be closer to worth while. Although since they sell other robots I guess that would cut into their bottom line.

This IS meant to be an educational toy, so it should be more educational, or not need to be put together at all and just be a toy. So if what you want is either a toy your kids will want to keep playing with, or a decent educationally toy, buy something else. We're hoping to find ways to experiment with ours, or at least hope the cats will find it fun.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8

Playroom Entertainment Ascension Deckbuilding Game: Ascension Eternal The game itself is pretty fun. It's quick to learn for a strategy card game and fun to play. A good variety in cards means no two games are really ever going to be exactly the same. There really isn't anything bad I can think of to say about the game play itself, I've had nothing buy fun playing it and I have played it a lot. The art work is all very nice and fitting to the setting.

There were however some quality issues with my set. Four of the same card is misprinted with the wrong type written, which was quite confusing and took some time to figure out. When packaged, the cards are split into two slots in a tray for storage, and then plastic gems added in one of the two slots. The gems are very sharp and pokey, and there was so little room, the gems stabbed the top card a whole bunch, which makes it look very ugly and you can tell what card it is before it's even drawn. This could have been easily fixed by putting more cards in one slot, as there was plenty of room, and then the gems wouldn't have been pressed so hard into the cards they were with. Lastly, my game board was misglued, and looks really bad, and it's the side you play on of course. Though, it is still useable.

I still would recommend it though, I don't see anyone else mention the problems I have with my set, so I'm sure it'll be fine, and none of those problems prevent play. As I said above, it is very fun.
text_fidelity_b: Playroom Entertainment Ascension Deckbuilding Game: Ascension Eternal

The child makes the sound of the animal that lands in fornt of the barn door  and places it inside the barn. If the rooster is the selected animal, one of the animals iw awoken and removed from the barn. cute concept but the plastic animal pieces are difficult to insert and almost impossible to remove. I am all for secure pieces to guard against loss but as an adult, I could barely remove them. Ther is some entertainment value in spinning the ring but it gets oild fast. MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys The box says that this Magnet Building Sticks set is for ages six and up, but I'm really enjoying playing with it as an adult. I think younger kids would need some help to do the suggested building projects, but using the set to build things is easy. The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The balls are 1 inch across, and the sticks are 2.25 inches long and 1/4 inch across.

The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The more stable builds (which have many triangles instead of squares) hold their shape well as you build them. Some of the building projects that have a more open structure have a tendency to collapse during certain stages of building, and then they start to attach to parts that they aren't supposed to. It can be a mess to straighten out. Once I realized that this could happen, I was more careful to stabilize these open structures as I built them, so this hasn't been a problem since.

The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. The pictures show only the finished building projects, but they were not always clear about what went where when the lines overlapped in the picture. Still, I've been able to do most of the projects, and of course you can come up with your own ideas. Kids may become frustrated trying to figure out the pictures and prefer to make their own building projects. Overall, I've had a lot of fun with this as have a teenager and a tween that have played with it.

When you press the button with the club a lever comes down and the ball will rest on the tee. When you release the button the lever comes with and the ball remains. The it is time to tee off! The balls are wrapped with two strips of Velcro and the board is soft and fuzzy to grab the balls when they hit. You are given 12 balls and one adjustable club two club heads. No batteries are required. Wish there were two clubs.  The "tee" is flexible, so it doesn't break-off.  This is for plastic balls only, so don't try taking this out in the yard and hitting "real" balls with it.  Please Note:  If you hit this hard enough, you could "dent" drywall.  So if that is a concern, you might want to hang this in the garage.

Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother I have to say that my baby (and my toddler) liked this soother. I, however, wouldn't say it is very soothing. It has too much stimulation going on to be considered all that soothing. (Even the 3 calmer scenes are still very active, bright, and stimulating.

This thing eats batteries. It takes about a week for it to completely deplete the batteries. Do yourself a favor and either use rechargable batteries or the lithium batteries.

I like the way this soother attaches to the crib. I've had many crib soothers and this one is the best for attachment. It has a holder that attaches easily to the crib and the soother itself pops in and out so you can move it without uninstalling it every single time. (And since it is more of a toy than a soother, you'll want to move it.)

The buttons are fairly easy to figure out, but once baby can stand or reach the thing, they can easily push the buttons themselves and cause chaos. The baby doesn't know how it works, pushes the upper buttons and makes the image on the screen change, then baby gets mad because they want their image back and they've got no clue how to do it. But you can't get them to stop pushing the buttons.

The remote only turns the thing off or on. It can't change the image or pull up one of the scenes. So, if baby hits those blasted buttons and changes the scene and gets mad about that, you can't use the remote to fix that. You can only turn the soother off or on. (And turning it on, it goes to whatever it was on when you turned it off.)

Also, if baby gets excited and hits the soother, the soother blinks out. (It turns off and turns back on.)
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother

Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games From the first time I saw Fallout the board game on the shelf I knew I wanted it. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Fallout The Board Game (Base) | Strategy | Apocalyptic Adventure Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14 and up | 1 to 4 Players | Average Playtime 2-3 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a: Wit's End Game, A Challenging Trivia and Brain-Teasing Board Game That Tests Players Wits as Well as Their Knowledge. Classic Party Night Fun for Adults and Family. Ages 16+ If those in your family and friend group are the kind of people that watch documentaries and go to museums for fun, this might be your sort of game. The questions rely a lot on having random knowledge on a wide variety of topics, although those with a broad knowledge of science might have an advantage. But the questions also ask about history, geography, literature, art, broadway musicals, economics and sports. The Teaser questions are fun if you like riddles, just don’t overthink it. The game board is simple to figure out but fun to play. The questions definitely make you think, and are fun if you like a challenge. text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

You launch a car through the loop arrangement to hit the rocket and collapse the loop; then you launch a car to jump the gap and raise the liftoff ramp; and finally you launch a car to launch the rocket.

The Stunt set has clear instructions for assembly, and if you follow them carefully, the stunt works exactly as promised. The stunt is fun by itself, but also connects to the track in your existing Hot Wheels layout, if you have one.

The stunt uses standard Hot Wheels cars. It comes with only one car, but it’s best with three cars, so that you don’t have to retrieve the car after each stage of play.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Entomologist Doll and Playset, Blonde, with 20+ Accessories Inspired by National Geographic ... and my girls' too! (Ranging in ages 5-10).

PROs:
--product received is exactly as pictured (we all know online toy purchases can be a gamble)
--the 10 tiny bug pieces included in the kit (which my kids would usually lose within a week) are kept perfrctly in place because they attach practically anywhere upon the included tree, flowers, rock, puddle, and leaves (and are also removeable) so Barbie can also take them to her "lab desk" later to study under the microscope.
--The accessories included were very well-thought out (for example, there is an area on the tree where a butterfly emerges from a cocoon, various pollinators that can "help" the flowers, and Barbie can gather the bugs from the tree and take them back to her "lab desk" to study under the microscope). In other words... this is a VERY "open-ended toy," and as such, would be also be appropriate for learning environments (I homeschool two of my children and also substitute teach preschoolers so open-ended toys that encourage imagination and learning are a MUST)
--Tree and desk are both sturdy enough to stand up without support
--The concept itself is pretty innovative and yet simple: STEM-toy-meets-Barbie is really the best of both worlds and can help encourage a love of science (science IS glamorous and Barbie is gonna prove it haha)
--In my personal experience, it is autism friendly, ADHD friendly, and even adolescent-friendly (I have all 3, and they are having a blast with this toy as we speak)
--a great gift for both kids and classrooms

CONS:
--Yes, this Barbie is high quality (it'll never be mistaken for any Dollar Tree knockoffs) but do keep in mind that this is Entomologist Barbie, NOT Yoga Barbie lol. So tiny fingers might need adult help dressing/accessorizing her.
--Barbie does not stand on her own without support (as is the case for most Barbies).
--no caterpillars included (not complaing because there are 10 bugs in the kit, including the cocoon that turns into a butterfly which was an awesome surprise. But a catepillar in the kit would have been SUPER helpful for helping explain metamorphisis.) All in all, this product is well-thought out, and certainly the coolest Barbie that my "geeky science mom self" has ever come across, so in my book it still deserves 5 stars and honestly more if I could.

If you're on the fence about purchasing this for your budding scientist who happens to love Barbies, go ahead and be the hero and take the plunge.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Entomologist Doll and Playset, Blonde, with 20+ Accessories Inspired by National Geographic

Safari Ltd. Safariology The Solar System Arrived in a timely manner, only three days. A bit smaller than I expected even though there isn’t anything in the description concerning size. I like good close-ups but sometimes they give a false impression of size. But that’s going to work out for the 3-year old recipient that’s continually asking questions about outer space and the planets. Good quality and painted nicely, with maybe Mercury being an exception. Mercury is painted greyish and I always assumed its proximity to the sun would make it red, but what do I know?

I was also pleased to see that he quickly noticed that there were eight planets, instead of the nine that he expected. He had picked up on that somewhere, either through a book or perhaps a TV show. And to my profound relief it stated that this product is phthalate-free. No, I have no idea what that is either. Sounds pretty important though. I sure hope no phthalate was injured in the production.

We plan to make a mobile from this. I think that is pretty cool because it will always be within sight and not crammed into a toy box to be seen only once in a while. It’s also something I wish I had when I was a kid.

Lately he's been watching Daniel Tiger, which precedes Sesame Street. So, inadvertently he gets a dose of Elmo. He's learned who Elmo is and thus when I grab the diaper with Elmo on it he got into the habit of squealing, ELMO! Thus, my reason for purchasing this toy. I thought that he would love this from "Santa." I could not be MORE wrong! My son hates this toy with a passion and I can see why.

My issue with Elmo is that he is too loud and jarring! There is no volume control, and you can't take him off to put scotch tape over his voice box. Which brings out another problem, you can't wash him because you can't his inner workings out. Another issue that I have with his loudness is that because Elmo has a high pitched voice, he sometimes hard to understand. My son's issue with Elmo is that he is too loud and jarring. (No, he's not Autistic) Plus, the fact that Elmo's mouth moves just creeps him out, which is my son's own peculiar quirk, but nonetheless adds to how much we dislike this Elmo.
text_fidelity_b: Playskool Sesame Street Let's Imagine Elmo

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs: Alien Slime Lab Science Experiment Kit & Lab Setup, 10 Experiments with Slime | A Parents' Choice Recommended Award Winner This is a pretty expensive science kit given what you're going to make - 4 very small batches of slime and a few "experiments" to go with it - but the value of the product is in the education your children will receive from doing it. Most slime kits are "here's the ingredients, now mix and play". This one gives you the ingredients, tells you to mix, and then gives you a "scalpel" and tells you to go to work.

This is a safe kit that is fine for the age range indicated on the box, although young scientists are probably going to need assistance from Mom and Dad on a few experiements, because a few of them are tricky given the limited space in the instructon manual.

You're going to need to head to the store as well, so be prepared that not everything you'll need is in the box. Some items are very common, others are a bit more unusual.

Overall, this was our favorite slime kit, and a great learning tool.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs: Alien Slime Lab Science Experiment Kit & Lab Setup, 10 Experiments with Slime | A Parents' Choice Recommended Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway OK, first off - we really love Magic/Neo/Twister Tracks. We have a number of different sets. Recently we grabbed the one with the single car and remote, along with the Rocket Racers and an off brand, dinosaur-themed set. All of which were excellent! This however, has a major flaw.

The jump ramp seems like an afterthought. It looks nothing like the picture on the box. It's like the box graphics were designed before the physical product. Even worse, its the connection to the track makes zero sense, and the instructions are laughable to say the lease. Oddly enough, the ramp is able to move back and forth like a see-saw, yet, it's not meant to do that! It's a ramp - and it's supposed to let the truck fly off and onto the lower track. Here's the kicker: one side of the ramp is blocked, like a dead end, so the only way we got this to work was to lay the proceeding track over it so it the truck wouldn't be stopped. It's like the manufacture designed this ramp piece wrong. Between that, and the see saw spring built in, my bet is, this was meant to originally do something else, but it failed, so they left it that way and simply called it a jump ramp. At 29.95, that's a disgrace. This is the only set we sent back. Most of the high ratings you see are for the other themes (firetruck, police set, etc..), so proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway
